questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: university with a good reputation in a nice city with many students. It was important to have many opportunities socially with students fx for finding new hobbies and attending social events.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy since all the necessary information was send to me per mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, I went to the students office once to get some help and that was good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my room in a shared flat via a list on the host university`s website with mails of students who had space in their apartment-that worked out great and I was really happy to have roomies who could introduce me to the city and later became my friends. I also looked at "WG-gesucht" which did not help me, since not many people answer and you have to pay quite a lot of money to use it. I would always recoment looking for a room in a shared flat, since I think that student dorm room can be very anonymous sometimes and its nice to meet people that know the city, language and culture to get a full experience.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its great to see a bit more then only the campus, because some students stayed there a lot when their room was located there as well. Living off campus for me meant that I would see a lot when I biked to campus in the morning and also that I had somewhere to stay where I could think  about something else in the afternoon and relax, go for a run in the nature or just explore the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit chaotic with many deadlines starting very early in the semester before you go on Exchange. Often I didnt know what I had to do next and luckily a friend who went on Exchange with me could help me and I could help her. The whole proces took a long time, 3 months minimum.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mails  from the Erasmus coordinators that explained what was missing in the proces and could guide one through it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, I got every intership that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be early on planning your stay, check your mails often and dont hesitate to mail/call the Erasmus coordinators.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Since the students program was different to the one on my host university and the study structure is different they sometimes did not know our levels and that was challenging. But it is always good to have a list with you with scills you want to learn and show them to the person who is responsible for you, so that you can work it out together.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was okay, but didn`t fit completely to what I wanted to learn.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were intersting but not very student activating like they are at UCPH. It sometimed was very old-school fx without any questions to the students and without any slides and with a lot of hierachy, which did`nt make it easy to ask.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical stay at the department for anestesiology,  internal  medicine and surgery

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot in all deparments, but mostly in anestesiology and internal medicine, because it was a nice learning environment.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I could not join the sports groups because I didn`t know the deadline and it was sold out quickly.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: a lot of sports, choir, hiking trips

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Choir-because you meet a lot of other students and its fun
sport-because you will be more motivated

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the old town, the castle, museums, art galleries, go to techno partys/ concerts with other students, hike in the mountains especially on the "Philosophen Weg" or go for a run

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture was simuler to mine in many ways and it was easy to adjust

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Ask your roomates what their plans are and join for partys or coffee dates whenever possible. Try to meet with people for your courses. 
 You can also find many events in the Erasmus groups although that is not with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The priorities were differnet and their was not a good work life balance. Apart from that many people were nice but quite introvert so its good to start Conversation in order to understand them better.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The ambition that all students had in common

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-be good at the language or take a class before
-its good to talk about your/ your host institutions expectations when you start so you don`t get disappointed or uncomfortable if they ask to much
-try to do as many activities as possible to meet people form the city and other internationals

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look on websites to find other sport of music groups if you dont get into the universities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Become integrated, find great friend and learn many knew skills

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Get used to the different expectations to students and to the way the healthcare system workes as weel as the communication between the different groups

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
